upper_bound.quote: (standard; details omitted). In all cases $G_p$ is invariant. $\blacksquare$
upper_bound.witness: The whole content of the invariance obligation is the claim that for every positive integer t, t | α and t | β ⇺ t | α' = min(α,β) and t | β' = |α−β|; the text explicitly declines to prove it ('details omitted') and asserts 'in all cases' without treating any case (α = β, α = 0 or β = 0, α > β vs α < β). What would have to be proved, for all pairs (α,β) of nonnegative integers, is gcd(α,β) = gcd(min(α,β), |α−β|) (equivalently the divisor-set equivalence), including the degenerate cases where one or both valuations vanish and where they are equal; and then that the gcd of the whole 2026-tuple is unchanged since only these two entries move. None of this is argued.
upper_bound.load_bearing: The identification v_p(M) = gcd(v_p(a_1),...,v_p(a_N)) in Step 4 rests entirely on this omitted claim; without it the invariance of G_p, and hence the choice-independence of M, is unsupported.

parsed.notes: Correct explicit formula for M. Move description (min, |α−β|) and no-two-1s given; termination via product/zero-count with the 'at least one >1' induction is complete. The sole gap is the invariance lemma, which is stated and then explicitly deferred as 'standard; details omitted'.
